newsitem.title: ITALY: FORECAST - Bank of Italy to cut rates soon - analysts.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Bank of Italy to cut rates soon - analysts.

text.p: The Bank of Italy is expected to cut key interest rates very soon if as expected consumer price inflation falls again in April with hopes underpinned by a series of encouraging indicators, analysts said on Wednesday.

Producer and wholesale price data for February published on Wednesday came in better than expected with PPI up just 0.8 percent year-on-year against a forecast 0.9 percent and WPI up 0.5 percent compared with an expected 1.0 percent.
The figures came hard on the heels of February industrial production data on Tuesday which showed an unadjusted fall of 3.8 percent against a 6.4 percent decline in January.

Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi described the output figure as "positive". He noted that if the number of working days was taken into account, February data showed a slight year-on-year rise of 0.8 percent.

Italian share and bond markets have firmed on expectations of a yearly April CPI rate below two percent, down from an eight-year low of 2.2 percent in March, paving the way for the central bank to lower its 6.75 percent discount rate.
Ciampi reinforced hopes on Tuesday by saying inflation was seen falling to 1.8 percent in April.
Preliminary CPI data from 11 Italian cities are due to be released next Monday and Tuesday with final Italian April data published on May 6.
Gianluca Sanna, analyst at Stone & McCarthy, expecting an April month-on-month rise of 0.2 percent and yearly rate of 1.8 percent, said the CPI data made a rate cut much more probable.

"The PPI figures were very good and the CPI data will also be very good. The international climate is favourable, with a strong dollar helping the lira firm against the mark, and so conditions at the end of April are ideal. A cut during the rest of 1997 will be increasingly difficult," he said.
Giovanni Polastri of 4CAST in London said, "The Bank of Italy could cut rates after the preliminary data, or they could wait until the final data on May 6."
Mariarosa Tirolesi of Deutsche Bank in Milan said, "An interest rate cut after the preliminary data is possible. the cut will be 50-75 basis points depending on the lira's performance."
The lira has been trading below its central ERM parity of 990 per mark for several days. On Wednesday it was quoted around 984/985 per mark.

Marco Ricci of Centrosim brokers in Milan agreed with most analysts' forecasts for preliminary April CPI showing a month on month 0.2 percent rise for a yearly 1.8 percent. He said: "We see the Bank easing after the preliminary data and then the central bank will adopt a restrictive monetary policy."
A Reuter poll af analysts last week saw the central bank lopping another slice off official interest rates in the near term but many believed this may be the last easing in the cycle.
On average 10 out of 12 analysts polled forecast a 50 to 75 basis point cut which would bring the Bank's official discount rate to 6.25/6.0 percent.
The Bank's last easing, effective on January 22, was a 75 basis point cut from 7.50 percent, its third reduction since July last year.
